Currently I use rufus to put an iso file onto a usb hard drive and boot/install windows off of that and while I like the process currently it requires too many clicks so I was wondering if anybody had a bulletproof guide on setting up a near zero touch mdt that isn't from microsoft since their docs are a bit out of date and usually refer to mdt 2010 and don't really help towards making the image as light touch as possible since they kinda want you to use SC** to do that.
Anyone have a good guide on windows 7 deployment with MDT2013?

I've set up MDT2013 in the past and got a complete image setup including drivers and apps using a PXE boot.

The docs themselves are not out of date. They are a little light on what you need to do but they do work.

From memory the biggest problem I had was permissions on the folders.

Tell me what it is EXACTLY you're trying to do and I will see if I can help.

I used MDT2010 extensively. I haven't had a chance to play with MDT2013 yet. The closer you get to zero touch the more MS wants you to leverage SCCM. You'll need to use the MDT Database and do some scripting in powershell to get closer to Zero Touch. If you can't get a SQL instance to use the MDT Database then you'll need to do everything through the customsettings.ini. I had my last environment near zero touch.

What's your end goal looking like? I might be able to point you in the right direction.

I have written a guide on that exact thing, a zero touch installation. It uses the AutoUnattend.xml file created in Microsoft Windows AIK.

http://nerddrivel.com/2015/06/29/windows-creating-and-unattended-installation-disc/

You should note that with MDT you need the following software prerequisites though.

Other Software Requirements

The Windows Assessment and Deployment Kit (ADK) for Windows 8.1 is required for all deployment scenarios.

System Center 2012 R2 Configuration Manager is required for zero-touch installation (ZTI) scenarios.

System Center Configuration Manager 2007 R3, System Center 2012 Configuration Manager, or System Center 2012 R2 Configuration Manager is required for user-driven installation (UDI) scenarios.

You will need to setup and entire deployment infrastructure. Worth it but a lot of work.
